title: Is Active Persona Inference Necessary for Aligning Small Models to Personal Preferences?
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark, 'FamousPersona', measures a model's ability to align with the personal preferences of famous individuals. For the 'religion' axis, this involves generating responses to prompts that would be preferred by public figures associated with specific religious or non-religious beliefs (e.g., Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Buddhism, Atheism).
findings: Religion was one of eleven axes of personal preference studied. Among all axes, prompts related to religion showed the most diverse preferences and the least agreement among different personas, indicating it's a topic with a wide range of viewpoints. The performance of models on the religion axis was analyzed as part of a leave-one-axis-out evaluation, but it did not show statistically significant differences in generalization compared to other topics.
